problems.title: Unconstrained L-BFGS allocates a dense Hessian before the first iteration
problems.summary: First-order Optim methods allocate quadratic workspace for an unused Hessian. The constrained-path change in #910 does not cover the unconstrained method.

commits.title: Use a once-differentiable objective for unconstrained first-order methods

fix.why_together: The unconstrained adapter and its allocation regression are one change. This commit applies directly to the recorded upstream base.

draft.title: Unconstrained L-BFGS allocates a dense Hessian before the first iteration
draft.body:
For an unconstrained solve on OptimizationOptimJL 0.4.23, a first-order optimizer allocates space for a dense Hessian. At 2,000 variables one such matrix is 32 MB.

```julia
using OptimizationOptimJL, OptimizationOptimJL.Optim, OptimizationBase
f = OptimizationFunction((x,p) -> sum(abs2,x); grad=(g,x,p) -> (g .= 2 .* x))
p = OptimizationProblem(f, ones(2000))
solve(p, LBFGS(); maxiters=20)
bytes = @allocated solve(p, LBFGS(); maxiters=20)
@show bytes
```

L-BFGS only uses gradients. A warmed solve should allocate less than even one dense Hessian, but the unconstrained adapter constructs a twice-differentiable objective. Select a once-differentiable objective for methods that do not request a Hessian. Keep the Hessian and Hessian-vector paths for methods that use them. #893 records the original report and #1442 covers the unconstrained path.

problems.title: AutoEnzyme cannot generate requested out-of-place constraint products
problems.summary: Requesting a constraint Jacobian product can dispatch to an absent user callback. When a Jacobian is supplied, generated products should use it before differentiating the constraints.

commits.title: Generate requested Enzyme constraint products and respect user callback precedence

fix.why_together: This change contains both product directions and tests for callback precedence. It preserves upstream’s in-place differentiation helpers and seed buffer, and is independent of the Optim and MadNLP changes.

tests: OptimizationBase/test/AD/adtests.jl — generated out-of-place products and supplied callback precedence
AutoEnzyme in-place products use a user cons_j
validation.detail: 9 assertions passed with Enzyme 0.13.221, including comparisons to explicit Jacobian products and tests that a supplied product wins. Tested dogfood commit 586bf50360655f1725a369e01a290292066685b3.

draft.title: AutoEnzyme cannot generate requested out-of-place constraint products
draft.body:
On OptimizationBase 5.10.1, this out-of-place constraint has a known Jacobian at `[1, 2]`.

```julia
using OptimizationBase, Enzyme, ChainRulesCore
ad = OptimizationBase.AutoEnzyme()
f = OptimizationFunction{false}((x,p) -> sum(x), ad; cons=(x,p) -> [sum(abs2,x)])
x = [1.0, 2.0]
g = OptimizationBase.instantiate_function(f, x, ad, nothing, 1; cons_vjp=true, cons_jvp=true)
g.cons_vjp(x, [1.0])       # expected [2.0, 4.0]
g.cons_jvp(x, [0.0, 1.0])  # expected [4.0]
```

Upstream selects a callback that was never supplied. Handle the two directions independently. Use an explicit product first, then a supplied Jacobian, then Enzyme’s reverse or forward differentiation with correctly sized buffers. #1410 and #1419 track the issue and proposed fix.

problems.title: Keep the solver’s multiplier vector intact after an in-place constraint pullback
problems.summary: Reverse differentiation used to clear the caller’s output seed. Upstream #1424 already copies that seed into a dedicated buffer. The fork adds an explicit assertion that the caller’s values survive.

commits.title: Assert that the in-place pullback preserves the caller’s seed

fix.why_together: The upstream base already includes the implementation. This one test-only commit covers the remaining difference from the topic branch. On an older base the original implementation and test were published together on that topic.

tests: In-place constraint VJP with a caller-owned multiplier and a known gradient
validation.detail: Both checks passed with Enzyme 0.13.221. The pullback produced the correct derivative and the original multiplier retained its value. Tested dogfood commit 586bf50360655f1725a369e01a290292066685b3.

problems.title: Allow MadNLP 0.11 in OptimizationMadNLP environments
problems.summary: The old compatibility bound excluded MadNLP 0.11. PR #1439 merged the change upstream, so the dogfood branch inherits it directly.

fix.why_together: The single upstream commit updates the dependency range and wrapper version. It is patch-equivalent to the fork topic commit. There is no additional patch to apply to current master.

tests: Solve a one-variable quadratic with a binding upper bound
validation.detail: 3 checks passed with OptimizationMadNLP 2.3.3 and MadNLP 0.11.0, covering the resolved minor version, successful termination and the expected boundary solution. Tested dogfood commit 586bf50360655f1725a369e01a290292066685b3.
